chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad, from Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi, who said: He narrated to us Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Hassaan, from Abdurrahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Has come the command of Allah, so do not hasten it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate [with Him].'

He said: It is our affair. Allah commanded that it not be hastened until Allah supports it with three armies: the angels, the believers, and fright. His emergence is like the emergence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and that is His saying, the Exalted: 'As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, and indeed, a party of the believers disliked it.'

key_terms.أَمْرُنَا: Our affair (referring to the Imams' authority and emergence)

ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Atha amrullah' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Al-Nu'mani records Abu Abdillah (as) interpreting 'Atha amrullah' as the divine decree of the Qa'im's emergence, linking it to the concept of *Taqiyya* and the necessity of patience during the Minor and Major Ghayba. The narration draws a parallel between the Imam's rise and the Prophet's Hijrah, noting that just as some believers were initially reluctant to the migration, some will be hesitant regarding the Imam's authority until Allah supports the cause with angels, believers, and 'fear' (rabb) in the hearts of enemies. This highlights the theological continuity between prophetic history and the eschatological role of the Twelfth Imam.
